HSTU’s official 2024 configuration provides a concrete sampled-softmax reference: 128 negatives, L2-normalized user/item embeddings, temperature 0.05, dropout 0.2 and learning rate 0.001. These settings motivate controlled objective/temperature/negative-count experiments within the existing HSTU, but do not establish optimal settings for these four Amazon categories. Strong training margins alone establish neither held-out ranking quality nor embedding collapse. [Official HSTU configuration](https://github.com/meta-recsys/generative-recommenders/blob/main/configs/ml-1m/hstu-sampled-softmax-n128-final.gin).

Negative-sampling correction depends on the actual sampler. RecSys 2025’s “Correcting the LogQ Correction” explains that in-batch sampling disproportionately penalizes popular items; its refined correction accounts for the positive being always included, rather than sampled. This supports testing sampler-aware correction when using nonuniform/in-batch negatives, rather than blindly applying popularity correction to uniform sampling. Correction remains approximate: a NeurIPS 2025 result establishes unavoidable bias for softmax estimators accessing only sampled classes. [LogQ paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.09331), [bias result](https://papers.neurips.cc/paper_files/paper/2025/hash/42b7c2f6d320d1fe1afa899a6319d6d7-Abstract-Conference.html).

For a ranking-oriented alternative, 2024 research develops sampled-batch WARP and LambdaRank with corrected rank estimates and reports improved recommendation quality. Practical inference: compare normalized sampled softmax, sampler-corrected softmax, and a corrected ranking objective through separate trials, each retaining one trained HSTU per category. Select using the fixed macro validation HR@10 against 99 unique negatives; published retrieval improvements do not establish gains under that particular candidate protocol. [Corrected ranking estimates](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.06371).
